error_1.title: What is an Error?
error_1.prompt: When we do something wrong in the code, Python...
error_1.explanation: When something goes wrong, Python stops everything and warns you! 🚨 This helps you find and fix problems.
options: Stops and shows an error message

error_2.title: try and except
error_2.prompt: We can use try/except to prevent the program from stopping when there's an error.
error_2.explanation: That's it! try/except is like a safety net 🥅. If something goes wrong inside the try, the except catches the problem and the program continues!

error_3.title: Division Error
error_3.prompt: What happens if we try to divide by zero?
error_3.explanation: Dividing by zero is impossible! 🚫 Python warns with ZeroDivisionError. Use try/except to handle this case!

error_4.title: Protecting the Code
error_4.prompt: Complete the code to handle the division by zero error:
error_4.explanation: try is where you put the code that might cause an error. If it goes wrong, except takes care of it! 🛡️

error_5.title: Safe Conversion
error_5.prompt: Complete to handle the error when the user doesn't type a number:
error_5.explanation: If the user types "abc" instead of a number, int() throws an error. The except catches this error and shows a friendly message! 😊

error_6.title: Error Type
error_6.prompt: If we try to do int("abc"), what error happens?
error_6.explanation: ValueError means the value is wrong! "abc" cannot become a number. Python warns exactly about the type of problem! 🔍

error_parsons_1.title: Safe Calculator
error_parsons_1.prompt: Assemble the code to divide with error protection:
error_parsons_1.explanation: The try comes first, then the dangerous code (indented), and the except last!

error_7.title: Text + Number = ?
error_7.prompt: What happens if we try to do: print("Hello" + 5)?
error_7.explanation: Python doesn't know how to add text with a number! It gets confused and gives a TypeError. Use str(5) to fix it! 😵‍💫

error_8.title: Ghost Variable
error_8.prompt: What happens if we use `print(x)` but the variable `x` wasn't created?
error_8.explanation: Python will say: "Who is x? I don't know!". This generates a NameError because the name hasn't been defined. 👻

error_9.title: Out of Bounds
error_9.prompt: If the list has 3 items, what happens if we try to access index 10?
error_9.explanation: IndexError! Python tried to fetch item 10, but the list ended earlier. It's like trying to read page 100 of a 10-page book! 📖

error_10.title: No Problems
error_10.prompt: If the code in the `try` does NOT cause an error, what happens to the `except`?
error_10.explanation: The `except` only works if there are problems! If everything goes well in the `try`, Python skips the `except`. Well-deserved break! 🏖️

error_11.title: Short List
error_11.prompt: Protect the code in case the list doesn't have item 10 (IndexError):
error_11.explanation: `IndexError` happens when we try to grab an item that doesn't exist in the list. With `try/except`, we prevent the program from crashing! 🛡️

error_12.title: Catching the Right Error
error_12.prompt: To catch ONLY the division by zero error, we use:
error_12.explanation: It's better to be specific! `except ZeroDivisionError:` catches only division errors, letting other errors pass so you can see them. 🎯

error_13.title: Non-existent Key
error_13.prompt: What error happens if we try to access `dic["chave"]` and the key doesn't exist?
error_13.explanation: KeyError means "Key Error". It happens when we try to use a key that is not in the dictionary! 🔑❌

error_14.title: Always Executes
error_14.prompt: Which try/except block ALWAYS runs, whether there's an error or not?
error_14.explanation: `finally` means "finally". It runs at the very end, no matter what happens! Great for cleanup. 🧹

error_15.title: Multiple Problems
error_15.explanation: You can have multiple `except` blocks! One for each type of problem. That way you give the right message for the right error! 👨‍⚕️

error_16.title: Typing Error
error_16.prompt: Can `try/except` catch typing errors (SyntaxError), like forgetting the colon `:` ?
error_16.explanation: No! `SyntaxError` happens BEFORE the program runs. Python doesn't even start if there's a syntax error, so the `try` doesn't work! 🚫

error_17.title: Wrong Spaces
error_17.explanation: Python is very picky with spaces! If you don't align the code correctly, it throws an `IndentationError`. 📏

error_18.title: Text is not a Number
error_18.prompt: Handle the error of converting "ten" to a number (ValueError):
error_18.explanation: `ValueError` happens when the value doesn't make sense. Trying to turn "ten" into a number is a value error! 🔠

error_19.title: Ignoring Error
error_19.prompt: If there's an error, do nothing (use `pass`):
error_19.explanation: `pass` means "pass". It's like saying "never mind". The error happens, is caught, and the program continues doing nothing. 😶

boss_battle_11.title: The Anti-Bug Guardian
boss_battle_11.prompt: Use try/except to try dividing 10 by 0. If it fails, show "Impossible to divide by zero!".
boss_battle_11.explanation: The Guardian protects against bugs! Use try/except to catch the error! 🛡️
